segments.text: This episode is full of people worrying about how they look to someone else, and then making themselves miserable because of it.

segments.text: Claire meets Valerie, an old coworker she hasn’t seen in fifteen years. Back then they were on the same career track, but Claire left work to raise a family while Valerie stayed with the company. At first Claire assumes Valerie must be jealous of her husband and kids.
segments.tts_text: [a natural conversational storyteller] Claire meets Valerie, an old coworker she hasn’t seen in fifteen years. Back then they were on the same career track, but Claire left work to raise a family while Valerie stayed with the company. At first Claire assumes Valerie must be jealous of her husband and kids.

segments.text: Then Valerie casually talks about traveling the world, having lovers in different cities, and possibly getting a huge promotion in Paris.
segments.tts_text: [a storyteller building gentle suspense] Then Valerie casually talks about traveling the world, having lovers in different cities, and possibly getting a huge promotion in Paris.

segments.text: When Valerie gets the promotion, Claire suddenly feels like the one being judged. She convinces herself that Valerie pities her, so she invites her home to prove that family life is amazing.
segments.tts_text: [a storyteller with playful humor] When Valerie gets the promotion, Claire suddenly feels like the one being judged. She convinces herself that Valerie pities her, so she invites her home to prove that family life is amazing.

segments.text: Valerie could not arrive at a worse time. The water is shut off, Luke spills bags of bottles from his recycling drive, and the house smells like alcohol. Alex is chasing a rat. Haley and Dylan are fighting on the stairs.
segments.tts_text: [an animated storyteller explaining the scene] Valerie could not arrive at a worse time. The water is shut off, Luke spills bags of bottles from his recycling drive, and the house smells like alcohol. Alex is chasing a rat. Haley and Dylan are fighting on the stairs.

segments.text: Phil is outside dealing with a portable toilet while trying to save a house sale. Claire watches the entire picture she wanted to show off fall apart in front of Valerie.

segments.text: After Valerie leaves, Claire explodes at everyone and storms out. When she comes back later, the family is sitting around the table eating together. Nobody gives her a speech or demands an apology. They just make room for her.

segments.text: That quiet moment is enough to remind Claire why she chose this life in the first place.

segments.text: Meanwhile, Jay agrees to play racquetball with Cameron. Jay is uncomfortable about changing in a locker room with a gay man and keeps imagining Cameron is going to look at him differently. Then, while they’re changing, their bare backsides accidentally touch.

segments.text: Cameron casually calls it a “moon landing.” Jay acts like it’s no big deal, but it completely gets into his head and ruins his game.
segments.tts_text: [a storyteller building gentle suspense] Cameron casually calls it a “moon landing.” Jay acts like it’s no big deal, but it completely gets into his head and ruins his game.

segments.text: Jay demands a rematch and wins. Back in the locker room, he tries to prove he’s over the whole thing—then realizes the man standing behind him isn’t Cameron at all, and suddenly he wants out of there as fast as possible.

segments.text: Mitchell has his own problem with Gloria. She’s been in a car accident, and Jay asks Mitchell to help because he’s a lawyer. Mitchell is pleased that his father finally seems to respect him professionally, until Manny quietly reveals that Gloria caused the accident.

segments.text: Jay already knew. He only brought Mitchell in because he didn’t want to be the one who told Gloria she was wrong.

segments.text: Mitchell tries anyway. Gloria gets defensive and fires him. Later she comes back, admits the accident may have been partly her fault, and asks for his help again—because she has already had another accident.

segments.text: By the end, Claire’s life still looks chaotic next to Valerie’s. She just stops needing it to look better.
